primary_data_sources.scope: Canonical human CYP carcinogen Km/Vmax review used to anchor Phase I expansion curation

primary_data_sources.source: PharmGKB VIP summaries / ClinPGx gene dossiers
primary_data_sources.scope: Allele-function and clinical interpretation support for NAT1/NAT2, GSTM1/GSTT1/GSTP1, ALDH2, UGT1A1, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP2D6
Class-specific pathway context and carcinogen activation/detoxification framing across the exposure classes
Benzene, NDMA, trichloroethylene, vinyl chloride, and related toxicokinetic anchor values already cited in the interaction model

expansion_backlog.description: Requested interaction-model expansion backlog. Separates the originally proposed 70-pair note into enzymes already parameterized in the competitive JSON versus enzymes still pending curation.

phase_I_cyps.notes: CYP1B1 and CYP2A6 are already in the competitive inhibition matrix; CYP3A5 and EPHX1 remain to be curated.

alcohol_aldehyde.notes: Alcohol/aldehyde kinetics exist elsewhere in the codebase, but these enzymes are not yet represented as competitive interaction pairs in this JSON.

steroid_androgen.notes: These enzymes are scaffolded in the broader ExposoGraph tissue and reference layers but not yet parameterized here.

phase_II_conjugation.notes: Most requested Phase II enzymes are already in the competitive matrix; COMT and NQO1 remain pending.

metals.notes: Metal-handling genes already appear in tissue and kinetic modules, but not yet as competitive interaction pairs.

ahr_regulatory.notes: AHR and ARNT should be modeled as transcriptional regulators for induction logic, not as Michaelis-Menten competition substrates.

niche.notes: Niche exposure modifiers identified for later curation.

scientific_validity_triage.description: Traffic-light review of the requested Tier A / Tier B Ki-curation list. Green entries fit the current Michaelis-Menten competition layer; yellow entries are biologically plausible but need tighter enzyme-substrate evidence before addition; red entries should be excluded or renamed because they are products, regulators, or otherwise mismatched to the competition model.
scientific_validity_triage.requested_priority_pairs_note: The enumerated Tier A / Tier B list sums to 36 pairs (21 Tier A + 15 Tier B), even though the surrounding note described 34.

green_direct_competition_candidates.rationale: Canonical direct PAH activation substrate for CYP1A1.
Direct CYP1A1 PAH activation substrate already represented in the competition matrix.
Direct HCA activation substrate for CYP1A2.
Direct HCA activation substrate for CYP1A2.
Direct nitrosamine substrate already modeled at CYP1A2.
Direct CYP1A2 PAH substrate, even though CYP1A1 remains the dominant BaP activator.
Parent estradiol is the competition substrate; JSON should use the explicit substrate name rather than shorthand.
Canonical extrahepatic PAH activation substrate for CYP1B1.
Direct DMBA activation step already represented for CYP1B1.
Canonical CYP2E1 aromatic-solvent substrate.
Canonical high-affinity CYP2E1 nitrosamine substrate.
Canonical CYP2E1 halocarbon activation substrate.
Canonical CYP2E1 alcohol substrate and established competitive inhibitor at high concentrations.
Direct nitrosamine substrate already represented for CYP2A6.
Canonical aflatoxin activation substrate already carried with a measured Ki.
Canonical CYP3A4 probe substrate already carried with a measured Ki.
Direct CYP3A4 mycotoxin substrate already present in the competition layer.
EPHX1 hydrolyzes the reactive epoxide, so the epoxide is the direct competition substrate.
Direct glutathione-conjugation substrate already modeled for GSTM1.
Direct glutathione-conjugation substrate already modeled for GSTP1.
O-acetylation of N-hydroxylated arylamines is a direct NAT2 substrate step.
N-hydroxylated PhIP is a direct NAT2 substrate in the activation pathway.
Direct sulfation substrate already modeled for SULT1A1.
Catechol-estrogen sulfation fits the direct Phase II substrate model when encoded with an explicit substrate name.
Canonical aldehyde-detoxification substrate for ALDH2.
Canonical alcohol-oxidation substrate for ADH1B.

yellow_provisional_candidates.rationale: Biologically plausible minor nitrosamine route, but CYP2E1 is the canonical NDMA anchor and CYP2A6 should not enter the competition layer without direct human kinetic support.
Glutathione capture is plausible, but human isoform specificity is less canonical than the CYP3A4 activation step.
Aryl-oxygenated ABP handling is more firmly anchored to NAT and SULT activation than to GSTM1 competition.
Electrophile conjugation is plausible, but GSTT1 is not the canonical benzene-oxide competition anchor in the current model.
Reactive-epoxide capture by glutathione is biochemically plausible, but direct human GSTT1 competition evidence should be confirmed before addition.
Chromium(VI) handling in ExposoGraph is primarily a redox and GSH-depletion story; direct GSTP1 Michaelis-Menten substrate framing is weaker.
ALDH2 acts as a backup formaldehyde-oxidation route, but ADH5 remains the dominant formaldehyde enzyme.

red_exclude_or_rename_pairs.rationale: CYP2E1 produces acetaldehyde from ethanol; acetaldehyde belongs in aldehyde-detoxification layers rather than as a CYP2E1 competition substrate.
EPHX1 hydrolyzes the epoxide to the diol; the diol is the product, not the substrate.
GSTT1 forms DCVG during trichloroethylene conjugation; DCVG is downstream of GSTT1 rather than a competing substrate for it.

competitive_inhibition._description: Enzyme-mediated competitive inhibition between carcinogen substrates. Formula: v_A = Vmax_A * [A] / (Km_A * (1 + SUM([Bi]/Km_Bi for i != A)) + [A])

CYP2E1._description: Most contended Phase I activation enzyme. Substrate inhibition >100 uM for pNP (Kss=260 uM). Ref: PMC3933162

benzene.notes: Km range 50-100 uM; activation to benzene oxide leads to downstream reactive metabolites

NDMA.notes: Km range 7.5-22 uM; LOWEST Km so highest affinity — outcompetes other substrates at low concentration

ethanol.notes: Km ~13 mM; competitive inhibitor of NDMA metabolism at high (alcoholic) concentrations. Also substrate inhibition.

vinyl_chloride.notes: Km ~100 uM; activated to carcinogenic chloroethylene oxide

acetaminophen.notes: Km ~1.3 mM; forms toxic NAPQI — relevant for GSH depletion at toxic doses

chloroform.notes: Km ~460 uM; oxidative dehalogenation to phosgene (reactive)

styrene.notes: Km ~70 uM; activates to styrene-7,8-oxide genotoxic metabolite

trichloroethylene.notes: Km ~12 uM; one of the highest-affinity CYP2E1 substrates

NNK.notes: Hepatic CYP2E1 is a minor NNK pathway relative to CYP2A13/CYP3A4; high Km

p_nitrophenol.notes: Reference probe substrate for CYP2E1 hydroxylation; substrate inhibition >100 uM (Kss=260)

4_methylpyrazole.notes: 12-fold lower than NDMA Km; used clinically to block CYP2E1

substrate_inhibition.notes: Substrate inhibition occurs above 100 uM for pNP probe substrate

CYP1A2._description: Activated by AhR ligands (PAH, dioxins). Key for HCA and PAH activation. Ref: multiple

PhIP.notes: Km=79 uM, Vmax=90 nmol/min/nmol; N-hydroxylation is activation step for breast/colon carcinogenesis

IQ.notes: Imidazoquinoline from cooked meat; lower Km than PhIP

caffeine.notes: Km=0.082 mM; competitive with phenacetin, Ki=0.080 mM; used as CYP1A2 phenotyping probe

BaP.notes: Ultra-high affinity; preferentially metabolized when BaP is present — but CYP1A1 is higher activity for BaP

NNK.notes: Tobacco-specific nitrosamine; activated by CYP1A2 in liver

MeIQx.notes: Heterocyclic amine from cooked beef; N-hydroxylation is activation step

theophylline.notes: Therapeutic methylxanthine; competitive with caffeine at CYP1A2

4_aminobiphenyl.notes: Bladder carcinogen; N-hydroxylation by CYP1A2 (hepatic) is primary activation

smoking_PAH.mechanism: AhR-mediated by PAH/dioxin content of smoke — NOT nicotine

CYP1A1._description: High-affinity PAH activator. Expressed in extrahepatic tissues, induced strongly by AhR ligands.

BaP.notes: Highest affinity substrate; will outcompete PhIP at any physiological concentration

PhIP.notes: Km 94x higher than BaP; significantly inhibited when BaP is present

Dibenz_ah_anthracene.notes: Mapped from the legacy DMBA placeholder (removed from the graph; non-IARC-evaluated) to Dibenz[a,h]anthracene (IARC Group 2A). Km/Vmax carried over unchanged from the DMBA placeholder pending dedicated kinetic revalidation.

7_ethoxyresorufin.notes: EROD probe substrate for CYP1A1 induction quantification

TCDD.mechanism: AhR/ARNT → XRE binding; up to 1400-fold in pituitary, 1600-fold in liver

CYP1B1._description: Extrahepatic (breast, prostate, lung) AhR-inducible P450. Estrogen 4-hydroxylation yields catechol estrogens implicated in hormonal carcinogenesis.

BaP.notes: Ultra-high affinity PAH activation in extrahepatic tissues

Dibenz_ah_anthracene.notes: Mapped from the legacy DMBA placeholder (removed from the graph; non-IARC-evaluated) to Dibenz[a,h]anthracene (IARC Group 2A). Km/Vmax carried over unchanged from the DMBA placeholder pending dedicated kinetic revalidation.

4_aminobiphenyl.notes: Alternative aromatic-amine activation pathway in extrahepatic tissues

resveratrol.notes: Dietary stilbene; competitive inhibitor of CYP1B1-mediated estrogen hydroxylation

CYP2A6._description: Hepatic P450 responsible for nicotine and coumarin metabolism; also activates tobacco-specific nitrosamines.

nicotine.notes: C-oxidation to cotinine; primary nicotine clearance pathway

cotinine.notes: Secondary metabolism of cotinine; major urinary biomarker for CYP2A6 activity

NNK.notes: Hepatic CYP2A6 activation of tobacco-specific nitrosamine

CYP2A13._description: Lung-specific P450 with higher benzene affinity than hepatic CYP2E1 at ambient (non-occupational) concentrations. At ambient benzene concentrations, metabolism may be dominated by CYP2A13 and CYP2F1 in lung rather than CYP2E1 in liver.

benzene.notes: Km ~1-5 uM; ~25-fold higher affinity than hepatic CYP2E1. Dominates benzene activation at sub-occupational air levels (< ~1 ppm).

NNK.notes: Highest-affinity NNK activator in pulmonary tissue; central to lung-specific tobacco carcinogenesis.

NDEA.notes: Pulmonary activation pathway for inhaled nitrosamines.

NNAL.notes: Activation of NNK-derived alcohol metabolite in lung

methoxsalen.notes: Mechanism-based inhibitor of CYP2A13; Ki ~0.08 uM

CYP2B6._description: CAR/PXR-inducible hepatic P450; activates cyclophosphamide and some nitrosamines.

CYP2C9._description: Major hepatic P450 for NSAID and warfarin metabolism; polymorphic (*2, *3 reduced activity).

S_warfarin.notes: High-affinity CYP2C9 substrate; anticoagulant dosing depends on genotype

diclofenac.notes: NSAID with reactive acyl-glucuronide downstream metabolite

CYP2C19._description: Polymorphic hepatic P450 (extensive vs poor metabolizer). Proton-pump inhibitor and mephenytoin metabolism.

omeprazole.notes: Clinical PPI metabolism; CYP2C19 poor metabolizers have elevated plasma levels

NNK.notes: Minor contribution to hepatic NNK activation

CYP2D6._description: Highly polymorphic hepatic P450 (PM/IM/EM/UM phenotypes). Metabolizes ~25% of clinically used drugs.

dextromethorphan.notes: O-demethylation probe substrate for CYP2D6 phenotyping

CYP3A4._description: Most abundant hepatic P450; AFB1 and many drugs. Hill kinetics for AFB1.

AFB1.notes: Hill kinetics (n~2); sigmoidal activation; Km=49.6 uM

sterigmatocystin.notes: Mycotoxin related to AFB1; competitive with AFB1

midazolam.notes: Clinical CYP3A4 activity probe; lowest Km

erythromycin.notes: ERMBT probe; mechanism-based inactivator at high concentrations

cyclosporine.notes: Immunosuppressant; CYP3A4 metabolism saturates at clinical doses

1_nitropyrene.notes: Diesel-exhaust nitro-PAH; ring hydroxylation by CYP3A4

6_aminochrysene.notes: Aromatic amine PAH; CYP3A4 + CYP1A2 dual activation

NNK.notes: Secondary hepatic NNK activation; relevant at heavy smoking loads

chronic_alcohol_indirect.mechanism: P450-P450 membrane interaction with induced CYP2E1 (PMC7856178); mild suppression

CYP2F1._description: Lung-specific P450 catalyzing benzene ring hydroxylation; co-dominant with CYP2A13 at low air concentrations.

benzene.notes: Km ~2-8 uM pulmonary; hydroxylates benzene to phenol and downstream hydroquinone.

naphthalene.notes: Classic pulmonary CYP2F1 substrate; relevant for inhaled fuels and PAH mixtures.

3_methylindole.notes: Tryptophan catabolite; bioactivated to pneumotoxic electrophile in Clara cells

styrene.notes: Pulmonary styrene activation; relevant for occupational inhalation

phase2_conjugation._description: Phase II detoxification enzymes. Competition occurs at the transferase active site between xenobiotic substrates; depletes co-substrates (GSH, SAM, UDPGA, PAPS).

GSTM1._description: Glutathione S-transferase mu-1; highly polymorphic with null allele ~50% frequency in Caucasians.

BPDE.notes: Primary PAH detoxification pathway; GSTM1-null individuals lose this capacity. graph_node_id resolves to BaP (the parent carcinogen) rather than the BPDE metabolite node, matching the existing GSTM1->BPDE_GSH DETOXIFIES edge, already tagged carcinogen=BaP.

styrene_oxide.notes: Detoxification of styrene-7,8-oxide generated by CYP2E1/CYP2F1

GSTT1._description: Glutathione S-transferase theta-1; null allele ~20% frequency. Specializes in small electrophiles.

methylene_chloride.notes: GSTT1-mediated activation produces genotoxic intermediate; null individuals are protected

ethylene_oxide.notes: Industrial sterilant; direct alkylator detoxified by GSTT1

methyl_chloride.notes: Small-molecule alkyl halide; GSTT1 substrate for biomonitoring

GSTP1._description: Glutathione S-transferase pi-1; Ile105Val polymorphism alters activity against PAH diol epoxides.

BPDE.notes: Primary PAH detox pathway in lung; Val/Val reduces activity >2-fold. graph_node_id resolves to BaP (the parent carcinogen) rather than the BPDE metabolite node, matching the existing GSTP1->BPDE_GSH DETOXIFIES edge, already tagged carcinogen=BaP.

acrolein.notes: Cigarette-smoke aldehyde; major GSH drain in smokers

ethacrynic_acid.notes: GSTP1 competitive inhibitor/substrate; Ki=0.14 uM (Ploemen et al. 1990)

chlorambucil.notes: Alkylating chemotherapeutic; GSTP1 conjugation implicated in resistance

NAT1._description: N-acetyltransferase 1; polymorphic (*10, *11); extrahepatic aromatic amine acetylation.

4_aminobiphenyl.notes: N-acetylation competes with CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation; slow acetylators have elevated bladder cancer risk

isoniazid.notes: Canonical NAT2 probe substrate; isoniazid-induced hepatotoxicity linked to slow acetylators

sulfamethazine.notes: NAT2 phenotyping probe; historic ratio for acetylator status

SULT1A1._description: Sulfotransferase 1A1; hepatic activation of N-OH aromatic amines/HCAs via sulfation.

N_OH_PhIP.notes: Sulfation of CYP1A2-generated N-OH-PhIP creates DNA-reactive species. graph_node_id resolves to PhIP (the parent carcinogen) rather than the NOH_PhIP metabolite node, matching the existing SULT1A1->NOH_PhIP ACTIVATES edge, already tagged carcinogen=PhIP.

UGT1A1._description: UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1; hepatic bilirubin and xenobiotic glucuronidation.

bilirubin.notes: Endogenous UGT1A1 substrate; *28 polymorphism reduces activity (Gilbert syndrome)

gsh_depletion._description: Glutathione pool dynamics under multi-carcinogen exposure. Ref: PMC9412641
gsh_depletion.notes: Below 20-30% normal GSH, Phase II conjugation capacity drops precipitously. Non-linear tipping point dynamics.

biology_model._description: Sigmoidal extension used by gsh_depletion_biology_model(). Hill feedback synthesis (gamma-GCS product inhibition by GSH) plus Michaelis-Menten saturable consumption. V_max_synth is anchored internally by mass balance at baseline; no separate synthesis_rate is needed.
biology_model._param_notes: Ki ~1.5-2.3 mM (Richman & Meister 1975, gamma-GCS product inhibition by GSH). Km_GST is an apparent in-vivo value chosen so wild-type biology G_ss matches the linear model's 30%-impairment anchor at the same total consumption rate (~29 umol/h/g).

PAH_GSTM1.notes: BPDE + GSH → BPDE-GSH conjugate (1:1 stoichiometry). GSTM1-null individuals have no this pathway.

chromium_VI.notes: 3 GSH required per Cr(VI) reduced: Cr(VI) + 3GSH → Cr(III) + 3GSSG. Major GSH drain in welders/industrial exposure.

arsenic_methylation.notes: GSH-dependent methylation by GSTO1/GSTO2; each arsenic methylation consumes 1 GSH

BPDE_conjugation.notes: Direct BPDE conjugation with GSH — protective if GSH available

acrolein.notes: Major GSH consumer in cigarette smoke; acrolein is highly reactive with GSH

cadmium.notes: Cd binds GSH directly; ~2 GSH per Cd; also induces metallothionein as backup

ethanol_ROS.notes: CYP2E1-generated ROS (H2O2, OH•) consumes GSH via GPx; coefficient estimated per umol ethanol oxidized

acetaminophen_NAPQI.notes: At toxic APAP doses, NAPQI depletes hepatic GSH leading to necrosis

regeneration.NAC_rescue: N-acetylcysteine provides cysteine for GSH resynthesis
regeneration.oxidative_stress_inhibition: ROS inhibits GCL (glutamate-cysteine ligase) — creating positive feedback loop under combined exposure

enzyme_induction._description: Fold-induction of CYP enzymes by lifestyle/environmental factors affecting baseline metabolic capacity

smoking._primary_mechanism: PAH/dioxin content induces AhR → CYP1A1, CYP1A2, CYP1B1. NOT nicotine directly.

CYP1A2.mechanism: AhR-mediated by PAH and dioxin-like compounds in tobacco smoke
CYP1A2.notes: Mean 1.55-fold; heavy smokers approach 7.3x. Substantially increases HCA and amine activation.

CYP1A1.notes: Amplifies PAH (BaP, chrysene) activation in lung tissue

CYP1B1.notes: Extrahepatic; important for estrogen 4-hydroxylation → catechol estrogens in breast tissue

chronic_alcohol._primary_mechanism: Ethanol stabilizes CYP2E1 protein against proteolysis; also transcriptional at high doses

CYP2E1.notes: Chronic alcoholics show ~10-fold in monocytes. 1.5-fold mRNA at 6h with 50 mM acute ethanol. Creates positive feedback: more CYP2E1 → more ROS → oxidative damage → enhanced NDMA/benzene activation.

CYP3A4.mechanism: Indirect — P450-P450 interactions in ER membrane (PMC7856178)
CYP3A4.notes: Mild suppression of CYP3A4 by induced CYP2E1 competing for ER membrane resources

heavy_smoking_chronic_alcohol_combined._primary_mechanism: Additive AhR + CYP2E1 induction; also combined GSH depletion

TCDD_dioxin._primary_mechanism: Potent AhR agonist; highest fold-induction of any known inducer

CYP1A1.mechanism: AhR/ARNT heterodimer → XRE binding in CYP1A1 promoter
CYP1A1.notes: Tissue-specific dramatic variation; liver is primary concern for PAH activation

CYP2E1.mechanism: NAFLD-associated CYP2E1 upregulation via ketosis and free fatty acids
CYP2E1.notes: Relevant for non-drinkers with metabolic syndrome

genotype_modifiers._description: Population genetics adjustments to enzyme activity. These multiply the baseline enzyme flux.

null.note: GSTM1 deletion — NO GSH conjugation of PAH epoxides. Major cancer risk factor.
GSTT1 deletion — impaired detox of small electrophiles including ethylene oxide

homozygous_609TT.note: Near-null NQO1; benzene risk greatly increased

rapid.note: Fast N-acetyltransferase — HCA detox vs activation balance

slow.note: Slow N-acetyltransferase — reduced HCA detoxification in colon; increased bladder risk

interaction_rules._description: Higher-order interaction rules for combined exposures

known_synergies.name: Alcohol + Smoking → Oral/Pharyngeal Cancer
known_synergies.mechanism: Ethanol enhances mucosal permeability to PAH; CYP2E1 induction generates more acetaldehyde; AhR induction amplifies HCA activation

known_synergies.name: Alcohol + Hepatocellular Carcinoma (combined with AFB1)
known_synergies.mechanism: Alcohol-induced liver disease creates permissive microenvironment; CYP3A4 modulation by CYP2E1 alters AFB1 activation ratio

known_synergies.name: Benzene + Cr(VI) → Hematotoxicity amplification
known_synergies.mechanism: Both deplete bone marrow GSH; Cr(VI) inhibits PARP; combined DNA damage exceeds repair capacity

known_antagonisms.name: Ethanol competitive inhibition of benzene CYP2E1 activation
known_antagonisms.mechanism: High ethanol competes with benzene for CYP2E1 active site. Benzene activation reduced by ~62% in the DBTEX mixture model (PMID:11509752)

known_antagonisms.name: Caffeine + PhIP CYP1A2 competition
known_antagonisms.mechanism: Caffeine acts as competitive inhibitor of PhIP N-hydroxylation (Ki~0.08 mM for caffeine vs phenacetin); may reduce HCA activation
